// Check that the register layer does not register internal types with
// the factory under names commonly used by user environments, such as
// the bus item "reg_rw" of the register examples.

#include <systemc>
#include <uvm>

using namespace uvm;

class reg_rw : public uvm_sequence_item
{
 public:
  reg_rw( const std::string& name = "reg_rw") : uvm_sequence_item(name)
  {}

  UVM_OBJECT_UTILS(reg_rw);
};

int sc_main(int, char*[])
{
  uvm_coreservice_t* cs = uvm_coreservice_t::get();
  uvm_report_server* svr = cs->get_report_server();
  uvm_factory* f = cs->get_factory();

  // make sure the register layer is linked in
  uvm_reg_map* map = new uvm_reg_map("map");

  uvm_object* obj = f->create_object_by_name("reg_rw", "", "rw");

  if (obj == nullptr)
    UVM_ERROR("Test", "Factory could not create an object named 'reg_rw'");
  else if (dynamic_cast<reg_rw*>(obj) == nullptr)
    UVM_ERROR("Test", "Factory did not create the user class 'reg_rw'");
  else
    std::cout << "Created user class '" << obj->get_type_name() << "'" << std::endl;

  delete obj;
  delete map;

  svr->report_summarize();

  if (svr->get_severity_count(UVM_FATAL) +
      svr->get_severity_count(UVM_WARNING) +
      svr->get_severity_count(UVM_ERROR) == 0)
    std::cout << "** UVM TEST PASSED **" << std::endl;
  else
    std::cout << "!! UVM TEST FAILED !!" << std::endl;

  return 0;
}
